chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment regarding four persons who were partners in a camel. One of them hobbled it, then the camel moved off, toyed with its hobble, fell down, and was injured. So his companions said to the one who had hobbled it, “Compensate us for our camel.”
So he عليه السلام judged between them that they must compensate him for his share, because he had secured his share, and their shares were lost along with his share.

key_terms.أَوْثَقَ حَظَّهُ: he properly secured his own share
key_terms.بِعِقَالِهِ: with its hobble or tether used to restrain it
key_terms.شُرَكَاءَ فِي بَعِيرٍ: partners in ownership of a camel

ai.seo_question: Who is liable if jointly owned property is lost after one partner properly secured it?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning shared ownership and liability. It establishes that when one partner properly secures the jointly owned property, he is not held liable for the loss of the others; rather, his own share is to be compensated because he fulfilled his responsibility.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5399 - The Commander of the Faithful (as) ruled regarding four people who were partners in a camel. One of them tied it, but the camel struggled with its tether, broke free, fell, and was injured.
The other owners said to the one who had tied it, "You must compensate us for our camel."

So Imam (as) ruled between them, saying:
"They must compensate him for his share because he had secured his portion properly, but their shares were lost along with his.".
